Nagyhalasz Jewish Cemetery One

Jewish Cemetery · Nagyhalász, Hungary

Not demolished. The first of two Jewish cemeteries in Nagyhalász appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with tombstones through 1941. The Jewish community grew from 75 in 1848 to a peak of 312 by 1930, organizing formally by 1881 with a burial society, mikveh, school, and yeshiva. Fifteen Jews from Nagyhalász died in World War I, yet the community still faced accusations of treason, robbery, and violence during the postwar 'White Terror.' By 1944 the Orthodox community numbered 262; its members were deported to Auschwitz via Nyíregyháza, and roughly 40 survived. The community shrank rapidly afterward - 39 Jews remained by 1949, just 3 by 1963.
